descriptor: Precision engine parts plus aerospace and semiconductor machining
lede: A Bengaluru maker of crankshafts and connecting rods for two-wheelers and cars that is turning into an aerospace and semiconductor-equipment machinist. Its ADS business tripled in a year and has a ₹5,700 Cr backlog, while the auto core keeps growing in the mid-teens. Returns on capital are still middling and the stock trades at 76x standalone earnings.

short_version.text: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue +33% to a record ₹1,021 Cr at a 19.2% EBITDA margin; ADS (aerospace, defence, semiconductor) revenue more than tripled, and a ~₹1,250 Cr semicon order took the ADS backlog to ~₹5,700 Cr. Net debt is low after a ₹1,200 Cr QIP in 2024.

ROCE has stayed at 13-16% for six years; capex of ~₹500 Cr a year keeps free cash flow negative, and return on capital added since FY24 is only ~6% (much of the QIP cash is still idle). Q1 margins were helped by forex and export mix.
~76x trailing standalone earnings and ~42x EV/EBITDA, against 58x for Craftsman, 57x for Happy Forgings and 91x for Bharat Forge.

blocks.text: Sansera forges and machines critical engine and chassis parts: crankshafts, connecting rods, rocker arms and gear-shift forks for two-wheelers, cars, trucks and off-road vehicles, in India and Sweden. Its ADS division machines complex parts for aircraft (Boeing and Airbus programmes, an engine blisk), semiconductor-capital-equipment makers and defence. We use standalone figures, as Screener's link was standalone; consolidated revenue is about 13% higher.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

Sansera is executing well on a credible pivot into aerospace and semiconductor machining, with backlog to show for it. But the stock is priced as a high-growth, high-return business while its overall ROCE remains mid-teens; the payoff depends on ADS reaching its FY31 ambitions and lifting returns, not just revenue.
